3. Ensure you have added or ran the appropriate tests for your PR: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-testing/testing.md
4. If you want *faster* PR reviews, read how: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#best-practices-for-faster-reviews
5. If the PR is unfinished, see how to mark it: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#marking-unfinished-pull-requests
-->

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind regression

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

A couple of issues were discovered and they've been combined into this PR since they all need a backport.

For https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120758: Triggered by a race when a GET to /openapi/v2 is called between https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/controllers/openapi/aggregator/aggregator.go#L227 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/controllers/openapi/aggregator/aggregator.go#L230

Fix is to initialize the cache with empty data so aggregation won't have problems.

For https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120739: AddUpdateAPIService was adding and also updating the apiservice spec. The apiservice spec update should be done async by the controller.

Fix is to not update the spec in the addupdateapiservice flow during startup. This is handled async by the openapi controller.

I've discovered https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120878 while working on the above two issues: The code path when an apiservice exists and needs to be updated was not handled properly. I've refactored the CacheableDownloader to have an new function `UpdateHandler()` and call that in `AddUpdateAPIService()` if the apiservice already exists. I've also removed the `decorateError` function and integrated the better logging directly in the downloader.

I've fixed the `AddUpdateAPIService` flow and added integration tests to simulate the cases described in #120758 and #120739. Added additional unit tests to catch #120878. Tried to keep the changes self contained since we need to backport.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120758
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120739
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120878

If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.

Enter your extended release note in the block below. If the PR requires additional action from users switching to the new release, include the string "action required".

For more information on release notes see: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/release-notes.md
-->
```release-note
Fix regression with adding aggregated apiservices panicking and affected health check introduced in release v1.28.0
```

issue_context.title: OpenAPI v2 AddUpdateAPIService should update apiservice and not reset cache
issue_context.body: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/controllers/openapi/aggregator/aggregator.go#L222-L229 is missing the condition if the APIService exists. if the APIService exists, we should keep the cache while updating the handler.

review_comments: I guess buildMergeSpecLocked already called Get(), which meant a slow request / timeout of one service would keep the specAggregator#UpdateAPIServiceSpec loop from processing other API services. Is that new in 1.28 or was it existing?

specAggregator#UpdateAPIServiceSpec blocking for each apiservice is pre-existing. The controller is single threaded so the UpdateAPIServiceSpec loop processes one apiservice at a time in a blocking manner. builtMergeSpecLocked calling Get() is a new addition, it is only called for local apiservices and from observation local apiservices are very unlikely to block and cause problems.

> specAggregator#UpdateAPIServiceSpec blocking for each apiservice is pre-existing

does that mean this PR does not resolve https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120739#issuecomment-1725875180

> The issue occurs only after v1.28 may be because https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118212 changed c.openAPIAggregationManager.AddUpdateAPIService to download the latest spec synchronously?

when an APIService is added/on startup with existing APIServices, only AddUpdateAPIService is called. There was a bug where AddUpdateAPIService called UpdateAPIServiceSpec that was fixed by this commit targeting #120739: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120814/commits/61603d36d738dddf3a7f244e0f8630f9ebeeffaf.

UpdateAPIServiceSpec is called by the openapi controller and is not in the path for readiness, and we are essentially leaving the behavior of UpdateAPIServiceSpec unchanged from before the regression.

> builtMergeSpecLocked calling Get() is a new addition

Aren't we still doing that in the current state of this PR?

> it is only called for local apiservices and from observation local apiservices are very unlikely to block and cause problems.

Where is it limited to local apiservices? This function appears to only be handling *remote* API services (it short-circuits if apiService.Spec.Service == nil)

> Aren't we still doing that in the current state of this PR?

Yes, `buildMergeSpecLocked` calls `Get()` on local apiservices. The problem described in the issue is for remote apiservices which leads to your next comment

> Where is it limited to local apiservices? This function appears to only be handling remote API services (it short-circuits if apiService.Spec.Service == nil)

`buildMergeSpecLocked()` calling `Get()` is limited to local apiservices. The `UpdateAPIServiceSpec()` function only affects remote apiservices (as seen with the short circuit). `UpdateAPIServiceSpec()` is not called within the critical path of readiness (only AddUpdateAPIService).

For readiness: 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/apiserver/apiserver.go#L330-L337
The apiservice controller syncs all existing apiservices before closing the ready channel and calls AddAPIService for each existing apiservice:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/apiserver/apiservice_controller.go#L112

which goes through
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/apiserver/apiserver.go#L478

and then reaches openapi's AddUpdateAPIService.

> `buildMergeSpecLocked()` calling `Get()` is limited to local apiservices.

It took me a while to understand why that is true...
1. we populate a cache entry for this remote service here containing an error that the spec wasn't synced yet
```go
		specInfo.spec.Store(cached.Result[*spec.Swagger]{Err: fmt.Errorf("spec for apiservice %s is not yet available", apiService.Name)})
		s.specsByAPIServiceName[apiService.Name] = specInfo
```
2. buildMergeSpecLocked accumulates cached specs:
```
	for i, apiService := range apiServices {
		caches[i] = &(s.specsByAPIServiceName[apiService.Name].spec)
	}
```
3. buildMergeSpecLocked merges calling .Get on each one:
```go
	return cached.MergeList(func(results []cached.Result[*spec.Swagger]) (*spec.Swagger, string, error) {
		var merged *spec.Swagger
		etags := make([]string, 0, len(results))
		for _, specInfo := range results {
			result, etag, err := specInfo.Get()
```
4. the result we just included will just return an error:
```go
func (r Result[T]) Get() (T, string, error) {
	return r.Value, r.Etag, r.Err
}
```
5. which buildMergeSpecLocked will log and continue:
```go
			if err != nil {
				// APIService name and err message will be included in
				// the error message as part of decorateError
				klog.Warning(err)
				continue
			}
```

I didn't realize we were adding two different implementations of Get() into `specsByAPIServiceName`, and that the one for remote services had a non-blocking Get() implementation

you folks are confusing to read, `buildMergeSpecLocked` almost does nothing, the closure that it builds does most of the work ... asynchronously. But yes, otherwise

> I didn't realize we were adding two different implementations of Get() into specsByAPIServiceName, and that the one for remote services had a non-blocking Get() implementation

That's correct.
